subject: Media Literacy
title: Subscription and Paywall Models
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Subscription and Paywall Models.

hook.text: The New York Times has 10 million digital subscribers. Most local papers have almost none.

buildup.text: Paywalls ask readers to pay directly, aligning incentives — the news serves you, not advertisers.

discovery.text: Subscription models reward quality because subscribers cancel if the content isn't worth paying for.

twist.text: But paywalls also create an information divide — quality news becomes available only to those who can afford it.

climax.text: In a democracy, limiting access to reliable information based on income is a serious problem.

punchline.text: Good news costs money. Not everyone has it.

quiz.question: What problem do news paywalls create?
options: Quality information becomes accessible only to those who can pay
